title.narrative: Flexible TA facility – NECP development and Decarbonisation Unit design

description.narrative: As Ukraine fights to win its peace in the biggest war of aggression since WW2, energy and environment are among the greatest damages. As recovery of these sectors is an absolute need, the country wants to use momentum to lay necessary grounds to the long-dreamed-of modern economy. This to-be state is not something abstract, because Ukraine has been cooperating with the EU to transpose common goals and principles. Unlike before the war, the plans and aspirations have to become practical in the near future as the country doesn’t have a big portion of its previous infrastructure to rely on. Ukraine signed the Paris Agreement and became one of the first countries to ratify it, committing to decrease CO2 emissions. The country has further updated its task in 2021, aiming to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 65% compared to 1990 until 2030. Ukraine has been long following the path of Euro-Atlantic integration. In energy and environment, it joined the Energy Community Treaty and committing to a number of reforms, including the development and adoption of the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). The country later signed the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement and officially became the EU candidate. Ukraine delivered a lot of reform efforts especially in the energy sector before the full-scale invasion. However, the current challenge is times bigger as Ukraine has to not only reform, but to rebuild at the same time implementing all the reforms and commitments the way they are supposed to be done. Despite the fact that on its way of recovery Ukraine does not start from scratch, the need for resources is massive. This includes not only finance, but also expertise, vision, planning and coordination that combined can provide the needed result by synergy. Ukraine has done a lot of plans and strategies, but there is a need to have them integrated in the energy, climate and environmental sectors through the NECP. The country has experience of such exercise as it was developing its first draft NECP in 2019-2020 that however was not adopted. The second attempt to draft and adopt NECP needs to be successful as it has a central role to play in transforming large portions of Ukraine’s economy ensuring their recovery. G7+ countries and the wider donor community have supported such efforts initiated by Ukraine’s Ministry of Economy as the general coordinating body, launching the High-Level Advisory Group on the sidelines of the Ukraine Recovery Conference in London in June 2023. It is important to note that based on the Energy Community Ministerial Council decisions (2021/14/MC-EnC and 2022/02/MC-EnC) adoption of the NECP constitutes the obligation under the Energy Community Treaty and Energy Community Secretariat is tasked to provide recommendations to the draft NECP that are to be taken into account in the final version of the adopted document. In addition, based on the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Government of Ukraine and the Energy Community Secretariat, the latter is committed to provide support and assistance to the Ukraine's NECP process and to coordinate international donors under the High Level Advisory Group. In this context, the project in question will be implemented in coordination and consultation with the Energy Community Secretariat and guided by the NECP methodology as defined under the Energy Community Governance Regulation. It is even more important that not only NECP is adopted, but that it can be implemented. It is necessary to prepare resources, including expertise, capacity and finance to be able to quickly move from planning to delivering. As the EU announces its innovative Ukraine Facility Program, it will be designed in parallel and along the lines of the NECP objectives, policies and measures. It is now when it is extremely important to immediately lay institutional as well as intellectual basis both at the working and political levels for the development and later implementation of the NECP and transforming Ukraine’s economy to deliver on the goals of decarbonization.
